evidence.exact_quote: This document is the **single canonical source of truth** for the Puppet Master User Commands system — user-authored command presets that inject templated prompts into a run. All other plan documents MUST reference this document by anchor (e.g., `Plans/Commands_System.md#COMMAND-SCHEMA`) rather than restating command definitions, discovery paths, template syntax, or execution semantics.

items.impact: This is a sound ownership baseline that reduces duplicate command semantics, provided cross-owner references are kept current.
items.statement: Commands_System is explicitly the User Command SSOT while adjacent runtime, provider, storage, routing, widget, and GUI contracts remain owner-projected consumers rather than command-local redefinitions.
items.title: User Commands ownership is explicit and bounded

evidence.exact_quote: A User Command's invocation through the chat slash-command surface or command palette ultimately dispatches a UICommand (`cmd.chat.run_user_command`) to trigger execution, but the User Command itself is not a UICommand.

items.impact: Builders have a coherent dispatch boundary and should preserve it.
items.statement: The source clearly distinguishes user-authored content presets from developer-defined dispatch IDs and names cmd.chat.run_user_command as the bridge instead of making each preset a UICommand.
items.title: User Commands and UICommands are not conflated

evidence.exact_quote: - Frontmatter examples preserve description, persona, mode, model, subtask, permissions_profile_override, and override_builtin.
- persona_override, mode_override, model_override, and permissions_profile_override remain requested overrides subject to their owner systems.

items.impact: Independent implementations will write incompatible files or silently ignore execution-critical overrides and subtask behavior.
items.statement: The canonical example and preservation criteria use persona, mode, model, and subtask, while the field contract uses persona_override, mode_override, and model_override and omits subtask; the example also omits the required name field. A parser, serializer, GUI, and migration cannot infer whether aliases are accepted, rejected, or normalized.
items.title: Frontmatter has mutually incompatible canonical field sets

evidence.exact_quote: - Invocation arguments substitute placeholders before file includes and shell injections.
- "@path file includes resolve with permission checks before shell injections."

items.impact: Untrusted invocation text or file content can be interpreted as a new file read or shell execution under one plausible implementation.
items.statement: Arguments are substituted before include and shell scans, and included file text is inserted before shell injection. The contract never says whether syntax introduced by an argument or included file is inert data or is reparsed as @path or !`command`; it also defines no literal escaping syntax.
items.title: Sequential template expansion does not define token inertness

evidence.exact_quote: - "@path/to/file includes the referenced file contents during template resolution."
- "@path/to/dir includes a directory listing."

items.impact: Permission checks can be bypassed or disagree with the opened target, and large or special files can hang, exhaust, or leak through prompt construction.
items.statement: The include contract does not define the base directory for relative paths, canonicalization before permission matching, traversal and symlink handling, TOCTOU behavior, binary/encoding failures, deterministic directory ordering, recursion, entry/byte limits, cancellation, or redaction of sensitive paths.
items.title: File include resolution lacks containment, determinism, and resource limits

evidence.exact_quote: - The pattern !`shell-command` executes the shell command and injects stdout during template resolution.
- deny, once, for session, and always responses follow Permissions_System ask flow semantics.

items.impact: A permitted command can hang, flood memory, leave child processes, conceal failure, or inject misleading partial output.
items.statement: Beyond permission gating and stdout insertion, shell execution has no specified shell/interpreter, environment, cwd binding verification, timeout, cancellation, output cap, encoding, stderr or exit-status behavior, partial-output rule, secret redaction, process-tree cleanup, or audit correlation.
items.title: Shell injection has no execution or failure envelope

evidence.exact_quote: - inherit and then narrow the parent permission ceiling and compatible capability universe, including child capability narrowing before dispatch.
- For this command run, the override effectively replaces the Persona profile.

items.impact: A command may gain permissions its parent could not delegate, or implementations may diverge between reject, clamp, and replace behavior.
items.statement: Child work is required to inherit and narrow the parent permission ceiling, but permissions_profile_override effectively replaces the Persona profile. The command contract does not state that the replacement is intersected with the parent ceiling or what happens when the profile is missing, malformed, changed during execution, or attempts to widen authority.
items.title: Permission profile replacement is not explicitly intersected with the parent ceiling

evidence.exact_quote: The preview does NOT execute any run. Shell injections in preview mode execute the shell command (subject to `bash` permission) but do not submit the result to any agent.

items.impact: A user can trigger mutation or external publication while believing Preview is non-executing.
items.statement: Preview promises no run submission but explicitly executes shell commands. Permission approval does not make arbitrary shell execution side-effect-free, and the UI contract provides no stronger warning, separate consent, sandbox, read-only restriction, cancellation, or side-effect result state.
items.title: Preview is labeled dry-run while executing real shell side effects

evidence.exact_quote:
Required behavior:
- resolve requested and effective Persona/runtime/model/effort state using the same pipeline as any other child run.
- classify the child dependency as `required` or `/optional`; `required` is the safer default for command subtasks unless the command explicitly declares advisory behavior.
- inherit and then narrow the parent permission ceiling and compatible capability universe, including child capability narrowing before dispatch.
- record the parent-child linkage in canonical event and storage records.
- do not silently fallback when the command explicitly requested a runtime surface that is unavailable or incompatible; this is the command-level `no-silent-fallback` rule.
- record the requested-vs-effective (`/effective`) provider `/runtime` surface when policy, availability, compatibility, or account binding changes the launched child.
- borrow provider child-session/delegation patterns where useful, but never require provider-native `session-tree` semantics on direct providers. PM canonical child-run identity remains the SSOT even when the provider has no native session tree.

items.impact: The intended feature breadth is visible, although several contracts remain contradictory or incomplete as captured by separate findings.
items.statement: The second prologue continuation specifies child-run resolution, permission approvals, management UI, preview, reserved slash behavior, UICommand dispatch, OpenCode deltas, and AC-CMD01 through AC-CMD10.
items.title: Core execution, permissions, GUI, reserved commands, dispatch, baseline, and acceptance surfaces are enumerated

evidence.exact_quote: | **Assistant chat** | Slash-command prefix `/` | User types `/<command-name>` (or `/x-<command-name>` for custom). Autocomplete popup lists available commands alongside reserved slash commands (`Plans/assistant-chat-design.md` §5). |
- Name is bold with /x- prefix shown.

items.impact: Autocomplete, palette dispatch, storage lookup, collision rejection, and displayed identity can target different commands.
items.statement: The source permits /<command-name> or /x-<command-name>, while the GUI always shows an /x- prefix and storage resolves raw <name>.md. It never specifies whether both invocations are aliases, which form cmd.chat.run_user_command receives, how reserved collisions apply after normalization, or whether names beginning x- are double-prefixed.

evidence.exact_quote:
- STORAGE-LAYOUT remains the anchor for User Command storage layout.
  - Project-local commands live at <project_root>/.puppet-master/commands/<name>.md and are available only when that project is active.
  - Global commands live at ~/.config/puppet-master/commands/<name>.md and are overridden by a project-local command with the same name.
  - Resolution checks project-local commands first, global commands second, and returns unresolved when neither path exists.
  - Unresolved invocation surfaces display "Unknown command: <name>".

items.impact: The same command set can resolve differently by OS/filesystem or change mid-invocation without a defined state.
items.statement: The global root is fixed to ~/.config without specifying supported-platform mapping, XDG overrides, unavailable or read-only homes, case-folding and Unicode normalization, duplicate physical files through symlinks, watcher refresh, malformed-file quarantine, or atomic discovery snapshots.
items.title: Discovery portability and filesystem identity are unresolved

evidence.exact_quote:
A User Command file consists of YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown template body,
  with canonical fields for name, description, arguments, persona/model/mode
  overrides, permissions_profile_override, and override_builtin.

Command execution resolves the active working directory to the bound worktree
  root when execution context has is_worktree true and otherwise to the active
  project root, applying consistently to Assistant Chat, Orchestrator DAE,
  terminal sessions, and file operations.

items.impact: The intended processing stages are identifiable, but schema, expansion, containment, and concurrency findings prevent deterministic safe implementation.
items.statement: This group defines frontmatter and template behaviors, read/bash approval gates, worktree-root execution, thread-derived worktree names, relative file cards, and terminal cwd snapshots.
items.title: CS-014 through CS-019 specify file format, expansion, permission gates, cwd, and worktree display

evidence.exact_quote:
- Assistant thread worktrees use .puppet-master/worktrees/thread-{short_id}, where short_id derives from the bound thread_id.
  - If thread-{short_id} already exists, command handling appends a numeric suffix such as thread-{short_id}-2.
  - Existing orchestrator worktrees keep .puppet-master/worktrees/{tier_id} style directory names as compatibility lineage.
  - Worktree-bound edit and file cards display paths relative to the resolved working_directory.
  - File cards open by resolving the displayed relative path under working_directory with no special path rewriting layer.
  - Terminal commands opened from the same thread set terminal cwd to the worktree path and persist cwd_snapshot on terminal_session_record.

items.impact: Two threads can select the same path, commands can execute in an attacker-controlled directory, and persisted terminals can reopen an invalid cwd.
items.statement: short_id derivation and collision domain are unspecified, numeric suffix allocation has no atomic reservation rule, and an existing directory is treated as stale without ownership validation. Missing/deleted worktrees, symlink escape, concurrent creators, cwd_snapshot invalidation, and cleanup/rollback have no state transitions.
items.title: Worktree identity and suffix allocation are race-prone and not recoverable

evidence.exact_quote:
When subtask: true is set, command execution launches a canonical child run
  through the shared delegated-run contract with required lineage, storage,
  permission/capability narrowing, requested-vs-effective runtime evidence, and
  no silent fallback for unavailable or incompatible runtime surfaces.

Catalog-installed commands remain canonical User Commands after installation:
  installation writes through the same command roots, updates follow manual edit
  validation, removal is blocked or deferred when active references require it,
  and uninstalling a catalog item never silently deletes a user-authored project
  override that intentionally shadows it.

items.impact: The major state families are named, but their failure, cancellation, concurrency, and precedence edges are incomplete.
items.statement: This group models delegated child runs, Persona and requested/effective resolution, visible working-set retention, deterministic expansion order, profile precedence, and catalog install/update/removal behavior.
items.title: CS-020 through CS-026 define child-run, override, working-set, expansion, permission-profile, and catalog states

evidence.exact_quote:
- Child dependency classification is required by safer default unless the command declares advisory behavior.
  - Child execution inherits and narrows parent permission ceiling and compatible capability universe before dispatch.
  - Parent-child linkage is recorded in canonical event and storage records.
  - The no-silent-fallback rule applies when a command explicitly requests an unavailable or incompatible runtime surface.
  - Requested-vs-effective provider /runtime surface is recorded when policy, availability, compatibility, or account binding changes the launched child.

items.impact: Required work may be treated as optional, duplicate or orphan children may remain, and parent completion can disagree with recorded lineage.
items.statement: The safer default is required unless advisory is declared, but the schema has no dependency/advisory field. The contract also omits parent or user cancellation propagation, child timeout, dispatch rejection, event-written/storage-failed and storage-written/dispatch-failed cases, retry/idempotency keys, orphan reconciliation, and required-child failure propagation.
items.title: Child-run lifecycle omits declaration, cancellation, and partial-creation behavior

evidence.exact_quote:
- Command UI shows requested override, effective result, inheritance source, and policy remap reason.
  - Command overrides are explicit child requests, not bypasses around the runtime model.
  - Command mode overrides are capped by parent mode authority.
  - Command model/runtime surface overrides become explicit child requests.
  - Explicit requests do not silently fallback.
  - Requested versus effective runtime/model/effort fields remain visible when remaps occur because of compatibility or policy.

items.impact: Implementations can either violate no-fallback or unnecessarily fail recoverable launches while showing incompatible requested/effective states.
items.statement: The UI must show effective results after policy, availability, compatibility, or account changes, while explicit requests must not silently fallback. The source does not define which changes are permitted remaps versus terminal rejection, their state/event taxonomy, whether the user can approve a remap, or how unavailable inherited defaults differ from explicit overrides.
items.title: Policy remap and forbidden silent fallback are not distinguished

evidence.exact_quote:
- Command cards remain in the current working-set while they are latest active results in the current branch of work.
  - Command-launched child runs and command-produced blocks remain while they support the next intended action.
  - Items remain while participating in unresolved comparison, /approval/question/validation state.
  - Items remain while explicitly focused or /pinned by the user.
  - Items leave when a newer result supersedes the same purpose, the finding has been carried forward, or execution clearly moves to a different branch of work.

items.impact: Identical histories can produce different visible working sets, unexpected disappearance, or indefinite retention of sensitive command output.
items.statement: latest active result, supports the next intended action, carried forward, supersedes the same purpose, and execution clearly moves are not defined or ordered. The contract does not resolve pinned items when branches change, multi-window focus, concurrent results, retention across restart, eviction, or who authoritatively marks carry-forward.
items.title: Working-set membership predicates are not deterministic

evidence.exact_quote:
- Catalog-installed commands are still canonical User Commands after installation.
  - Installation creates or updates a command in the same canonical command roots described in section 2.
  - Updates follow the same validation rules as manual edits.
  - Removal is blocked or deferred when the command is actively referenced by an open edit session or another subsystem requires explicit replacement/confirmation.
  - Uninstalling a catalog item must not silently delete a user-authored project override that intentionally shadows it.

items.impact: Updates can overwrite local work, untrusted catalog content can become executable prompt/shell material, and failures can leave corrupt or ambiguously owned commands.
items.statement: The source requires safe updates and deferred removal but does not define catalog identity/version/signature, provenance persistence, merge/conflict behavior with manual edits, atomic writes, interrupted install/update, offline or stale-catalog behavior, concurrent editors, deferral states and retry triggers, rollback, or what counts as an intentional user override.
items.title: Catalog lifecycle lacks provenance, trust, concurrency, and rollback contracts

evidence.exact_quote:
The Commands settings screen is part of Settings > Rules & Commands, this
  document is the SSOT for Commands GUI behavior, and the GUI shows whether each
  command is local/manual, catalog-installed, or catalog-installed with local

The command editor Preview resolves a template with sample arguments and

items.impact: The main user journey is enumerated, but shadow state, save/delete races, accessibility, localization, and preview safety are not closed.
items.statement: This group specifies Settings placement, provenance labels, scope selection, the command table, create/edit/delete flows, inline validation, and rendered preview.
items.title: CS-027 through CS-034 define the management GUI through preview rendering

evidence.exact_quote:
- The table lists all resolved project and global commands.
  - Project-local commands are indicated with a badge.
  - Columns include Name, Scope, Description, Persona, Mode, Model, and Subtask.
  - Name is bold with /x- prefix shown.
  - Description is truncated to one line.
  - Persona, Mode, and Model show unset inherited states as specified.
  - Subtask true is indicated with a checkbox icon.
  - The table sorts alphabetically by name with project-local entries before global entries when names match.

items.impact: Users can edit, delete, or invoke the wrong version while believing both rows are active resolved commands.
items.statement: The table lists all project and global commands and sorts a project override before the matching global row, even though resolution makes only the project row effective. No disabled/shadowed state, effective-source marker, invocation target, scope-filter interaction, or behavior after live filesystem changes is defined.
items.title: The resolved-command table does not define effective versus shadowed rows

evidence.exact_quote:
- Row click opens the same editor pre-populated.
  - Edit button opens the same editor pre-populated.
  - Editing a global command while a project is active offers Save as project override.
  - Editing a global command while a project is active offers Save globally.

- Every save validates the command file against section 3 schema.
  - Inline errors are displayed for reserved name collision, invalid name format, missing description, invalid mode value, and invalid model format.
  - If override_builtin: true is set while the command name matches a reserved Assistant Chat slash command, inline validation explains that override_builtin does not apply to canonical reserved chat commands.
  - Save is blocked until errors are resolved.

items.impact: A valid UI save can silently overwrite newer content, create a partially written command, or report success while discovery still serves another version.
items.statement: Pre-populated editing and save-time validation do not bind a file revision, revalidate after external changes, reserve the name, perform an atomic durable write, or define write/rename/fsync failure and rollback. Save-as-override and save-global can race another editor, catalog update, or watcher refresh.
items.title: Edit and save have no optimistic concurrency or atomic commit contract

evidence.exact_quote:
- Delete button uses a confirmation modal.
  - Deleting a project-local command that overrides a global one reveals the global version.
  - Deleting a global command with no project override removes it entirely.

items.impact: Users can remove the wrong scope, unexpectedly expose a global command, or lose authored content without recoverability.
items.statement: Delete specifies only a generic modal and reveal behavior. It does not identify the exact scope/provenance/path and resulting effective command, reconcile catalog deferral and active references, require typed or severity-scaled confirmation, define filesystem failure/partial deletion, offer undo/trash, or record an audit event.
items.title: Delete confirmation has no dependency summary, failure state, or recovery
